title: Load Balancing
summary: Load balancing spreads traffic over many servers so no single one is overwhelmed and any one can fail without users noticing. It happens in layers. DNS picks a region, a fast Layer 4 balancer spreads raw TCP connections, and a Layer 7 proxy that understands HTTP picks a healthy backend for each request. Health checks keep broken servers out of rotation.

walkthrough.title: DNS picks a region
walkthrough.text: The client resolves api.example.com. Global server load balancing (GSLB) returns the virtual IP (VIP) of the closest healthy region, or an anycast IP announced everywhere.

walkthrough.title: L4 spreads connections
walkthrough.text: The TCP connection reaches a Layer 4 balancer. It hashes the 5-tuple (source/dest IP and port, protocol) with consistent hashing so every packet of a connection lands on the same proxy, even if a balancer instance changes.

walkthrough.title: L7 terminates TLS and routes
walkthrough.text: The Layer 7 proxy decrypts TLS, reads the HTTP request, and picks a route from the host, path, and headers, for example /api/orders → orders-service.

walkthrough.title: Pick a backend
walkthrough.text: Within the pool, it uses power-of-two-choices: sample two healthy backends and send to the one with fewer in-flight requests. This beats round-robin when requests vary in cost.

walkthrough.title: Timeouts, retries, circuit breaking
walkthrough.text: Each request has a deadline. Safe requests retry once on another backend within a retry budget, and a backend with too many failures is temporarily ejected.

walkthrough.title: Health checks
walkthrough.text: Active probes hit /healthz every few seconds and outlier detection watches real error rates. Failing backends leave the pool and return only after passing again.

walkthrough.title: Drain during deploys
walkthrough.text: Before a backend shuts down it is marked draining: no new requests, but in-flight ones finish. Rolling deploys then cause zero errors.

data.label: Clients

input.name: Response
input.type: HTTP response from whichever backend served it

responsibilities: Resolve the hostname and open connections to the VIP.
Reuse connections (keep-alive, HTTP/2) to avoid repeated handshakes.
Retry idempotent requests with backoff on connection errors.

failureModes.scenario: Client caches DNS far beyond TTL
failureModes.impact: Keeps sending traffic to a drained or failed region.
failureModes.mitigation: Anycast VIPs that move without DNS changes; keep old regions serving during cutover.

failureModes.scenario: Long-lived connections pin to old backends
failureModes.impact: New servers get no traffic after scale-up.
failureModes.mitigation: Cap connection lifetime; balance per request at L7, not per connection.

data.label: Global DNS / GSLB

output.name: Answer
output.type: VIP of nearest healthy region (TTL 60 s)

responsibilities: Routes users to a region by latency, geography, or weight.
Removes a region from answers when its health checks fail.
Enables gradual traffic shifts between regions.

failureModes.scenario: Region fails but cached answers persist
failureModes.impact: Some users keep failing until TTLs expire.
failureModes.mitigation: Short TTLs plus anycast, or client-side fallback hosts.

failureModes.scenario: All traffic failed over to one region
failureModes.impact: The survivor is overloaded and fails too, a cascading failure.
failureModes.mitigation: Keep enough spare capacity in each region (N+1) and shed load at the edge.

data.label: L4 Load Balancer

output.name: Forwarded
output.type: Same connection always to the same L7 proxy

responsibilities: Spreads millions of connections per second without reading HTTP.
Keeps each connection on one proxy using consistent hashing on the 5-tuple.
Often uses direct server return: replies skip the balancer entirely.

failureModes.impact: With naive hashing, live connections are reset.
failureModes.mitigation: Consistent hashing (Maglev table) plus connection tracking keeps most flows stable.

failureModes.impact: Connection tables fill and legitimate users are refused.
failureModes.mitigation: SYN cookies, stateless designs, and upstream DDoS scrubbing.

data.label: L7 Proxy

output.name: Upstream call
output.type: To a chosen backend in the matching pool, with deadline

responsibilities: Terminates TLS and routes by host, path, header, or weight (canaries).
Picks backends by load, not just turn order.
Enforces timeouts, retry budgets, and circuit breakers.

failureModes.impact: Every layer retries 3×, multiplying load on a struggling service.
failureModes.mitigation: Retry budgets (e.g. at most 10% extra) and retry only at one layer.

failureModes.impact: It keeps receiving its share and its queue grows.
failureModes.mitigation: Least-request or latency-aware balancing; outlier ejection.

data.label: Backend Pool
responsibilities: Serve requests without relying on local session state, so any instance can serve anyone.
Finish in-flight work when asked to drain.

failureModes.scenario: Sticky sessions stored in instance memory
failureModes.impact: Losing an instance logs users out; load cannot rebalance.
failureModes.mitigation: Store sessions externally (Redis) or in signed tokens.

failureModes.scenario: Health check passes but real requests fail
failureModes.impact: Broken instance stays in the pool.
failureModes.mitigation: Deep readiness checks and passive outlier detection on real traffic.

data.label: Health Checks & Discovery

input.name: Signals
input.type: Probe results, deploy events, autoscaling changes

output.name: Endpoints
output.type: Healthy backend list pushed to proxies

responsibilities: Probes every backend and tracks pass/fail streaks.
Publishes the current healthy endpoint set to all proxies.
Marks instances draining during deploys and scale-in.

failureModes.scenario: Checker network partition marks everything unhealthy
failureModes.impact: Proxies have no backends: a full outage caused by monitoring.
failureModes.mitigation: Panic threshold: if most hosts look unhealthy, keep routing to all of them.

failureModes.impact: Joins and leaves the pool constantly.
failureModes.mitigation: Require several consecutive passes to rejoin; hold-down timers.
